_meta.purpose: Curated problem→solution mapping (BETA — hidden behind ?beta=1). Every entry cites its source. Never generated by AI. Reviewed against classical sources listed below.
sources_consulted: Ḥiṣn al-Muslim (Fortress of the Muslim) — Saʿīd ibn ʿAlī al-Qaḥṭānī

_meta.notes: Each `solutions[].ref` must resolve to a real page on this site. `type` is one of: dua (data/duas/duas.json slug), ayah (verse-key like '2:255'), page (a static route slug). Every dua ref carries the same source as the underlying dua entry.

solutions.reason: The Prophet ﷺ taught this dua specifically for worry and grief
"Verily, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest."
"Allah is sufficient for us and He is the best Disposer of affairs." — the dua of the believers when tested
The dua the Prophet ﷺ said in times of severe distress
The Prophet ﷺ's specific supplication for the removal of grief, worry, and heaviness of debt.
The Prophet ﷺ taught this specifically for when facing an enemy or danger
Recited by the Prophet Ibrāhīm ﷺ when thrown into the fire, and by the Prophet ﷺ at Uḥud
Recite three times morning and evening — "nothing on earth or in the heavens will harm you"
'I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created' — the Prophet ﷺ's protective dua.
The Prophet ﷺ said this brings tranquillity when anger flares
'The strong man is not the one who wrestles well, but the one who controls himself when angry.'
The Prophet ﷺ taught seeking refuge from Satan when anger arises.
The Prophet ﷺ taught this dua for relief from debt — "Allah will remove even a mountain of debt"
The same dua covers helplessness, laziness, stinginess, and the burden of debt
The Prophet ﷺ's dua asking Allah for sufficiency from His halal against the haram, and independence through His bounty from all others.
The Master of Seeking Forgiveness (Sayyid al-Istighfār) — whoever says it in the day with certainty and dies that day enters Paradise (Bukhārī 6306)
The Prophet ﷺ sought forgiveness more than 70 times a day (Bukhārī 6307)
The dua of Yūnus (Jonah) ﷺ — "No Muslim supplicates with these words and is not answered" (Tirmidhī 3505)
A short daily repentance formula from the Sunnah
The 'Sayyid al-Istighfar' — the master supplication for forgiveness, whose reciter with certainty in the morning is promised Paradise if he dies that day.
Allah says: 'O son of Adam, so long as you call upon Me and hope in Me, I will forgive you whatever comes from you and I will not mind.'
"Our Lord, do not turn our hearts away after You have guided us" (Q 3:8)
"Guide us to the straight path" — recited in every prayer
Salat al-Istikhārah — the two-rakʿah prayer of guidance the Prophet ﷺ taught for every decision, big or small.
"O my Lord, increase me in knowledge" — the only knowledge Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ to ask for increase in (Q 20:114)

'Whoever travels a path in search of knowledge, Allah will make easy for him a path to Paradise.'

"Indeed, with hardship [comes] ease." — mentioned twice in Sūrat al-Sharḥ
The dua of severe distress
'How wonderful is the affair of the believer — everything is good for him. If ease comes he is grateful, if hardship comes he is patient — and both are good for him.'
"My Lord, have mercy upon them as they raised me when I was small" (Q 17:24)

Forgiveness for oneself, parents, and all believers (Q 14:41)

Gratitude for water — a great mercy

The dua of Ibrāhīm ﷺ: "And when I am ill, it is He who cures me" (Q 26:80)

"Whoever fears Allah, He will make a way out for him, and provide for him from where he does not expect." (Q 65:2-3)

'Whoever loves that his rizq be expanded and his lifespan lengthened, let him keep the ties of kinship.'

"Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us" (Q 3:8)

Ask Allah for comforting family and offspring (Q 25:74)

Hadith Qudsi: Allah says 'I am with My servant when he remembers Me, and I move his lips with My name.' You are not alone when you are remembering Him.
'Whoever draws near to Me by a hand span, I draw near to him by a cubit; whoever comes to Me walking, I come to him at speed.'
"Our Lord, grant us from among our spouses and offspring comfort to our eyes" (Q 25:74)
"Among His signs is that He created for you mates from yourselves that you may find tranquillity in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy." (Q 30:21)
'A woman is married for four reasons: her wealth, her lineage, her beauty, or her religion — choose the religious one, may your hands be dusted.'
The dua of severe distress — recited by the Prophet ﷺ in moments of intense grief
"Innā lillāhi wa innā ilayhi rājiʿūn" — to Allah we belong and to Him we return
Ask forgiveness for the deceased and all believers (Q 14:41)
'Patience is at the first stroke of the calamity' — the Prophet ﷺ's counsel to a grieving woman at a graveside.
The Prophet ﷺ taught the dua at hardship: 'Innā lillāhi wa innā ilayhi rājiʿūn — Allāhumma ajirnī fī muṣībatī wa akhluf lī khayran minhā.'
The dua asking Allah for sufficiency from His halal against the haram — foundational for anyone struggling with work or livelihood.
'Whoever is mindful of Allah, He will make for him a way out — and provide for him from where he does not expect.'
'And He will provide for him from where he does not expect. Whoever puts his trust in Allah, He is sufficient for him.'
'Whoever loves that his rizq be expanded and his lifespan lengthened, let him keep the ties of kinship.'
For clarity when weighing a job offer, a role change, or whether to leave a workplace.
The dua of Musa (as) before addressing Pharaoh: 'My Lord, expand for me my chest, ease for me my task, and loosen the knot from my tongue.' The canonical pre-exam dua.
'My Lord, increase me in knowledge.' The Prophet ﷺ was commanded to say this.
The full verse the pre-exam dua comes from — 'Say: My Lord, increase me in knowledge.'
'Whoever travels a path in search of knowledge, Allah will make easy for him a path to Paradise.'
The Prophet ﷺ's ruqya for children — 'I seek refuge for you in the perfect words of Allah from every devil and creeping thing and every evil, envious eye.'
'Our Lord, grant us from among our spouses and offspring comfort to our eyes, and make us leaders for the righteous.'
The Prophet ﷺ was asked which deed is most beloved to Allah — he said prayer at its time, then dutifulness to parents. Teach your child this order.
'And of His signs is that He created for you from yourselves mates that you may find tranquility in them, and He placed between you affection and mercy.'
'Live with them in kindness. If you dislike them, perhaps you dislike a thing in which Allah has placed much good.'
Ask Allah to make your household a source of coolness of the eyes, not friction.
'A believer must not hate a believing woman. If he dislikes one trait in her, he will be pleased with another.'

Allah says: 'O son of Adam, so long as you call upon Me and hope in Me, I will forgive you whatever comes from you and I will not mind. O son of Adam, were your sins to reach the clouds of the sky and were you then to ask forgiveness, I would forgive you.'
'Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves — do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins.'
Sayyid al-Istighfar — 'I acknowledge Your favor upon me and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins except You.'

The dua of Yunus (as) from the belly of the whale: 'There is no god but You, glory be to You, indeed I was among the wrongdoers.' The Prophet ﷺ said no Muslim calls on Allah with these words for anything except that Allah answers him.
'Perhaps you dislike a thing and it is good for you; perhaps you love a thing and it is bad for you — and Allah knows, while you do not know.'

'A servant's dua is answered so long as he does not ask for sin or for cutting ties of kinship, and so long as he does not become impatient.' The Prophet ﷺ was asked what impatience is; he said the servant saying: I have called and called and no answer has come, and giving up.'
'How wonderful is the affair of the believer — everything is good for him.' Whatever the outcome, it is being turned into good for you.
'Allah is sufficient for us and He is the best Disposer of affairs.' The dua of Ibrahim (as) in the fire — the ultimate 'I have done my part, now You handle it.'
